simple.meaning: זְבַן (zᵉban) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to acquire by purchase.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 2:8. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זְבַן (H2084) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: זְבַן (zᵉban) / H2084 is traced through Daniel 2:8 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H2084. zeban [ זְבַן ] verb buy, gain ( ᵑ7 id., buy , Syriac Old Aramaic, Nabataean, Palmyrene זבן (often) Lzb 266 SAC 47 , compare Assyrian zibânîtu , scales );- Pe`al Participle active plural זָבְנִין Dan 2:8 time ye (are seeking to) gain.

occurrences.englishText: The king answered, “I know of a certainty that you are trying to gain time, because you see the thing has gone from me.
